canonical_statement: A continuous-path diffusion with local characteristics determined by a second-order operator L is characterized in law by the associated martingale problem; the exact direction and hypotheses must be selected from a pinpointed primary theorem before formalization.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: finite-dimensional real state space R^d; continuous path sample space; time in nonnegative reals; Prop universe 0. Exact Lean universes are not frozen.
ordered_binders: diffusion coefficients a and b, or equivalently generator L
initial point or initial probability law
hypothesis_families_to_resolve: measurability and regularity of a and b
test-function class, commonly compactly supported twice continuously differentiable functions
integrability needed for martingale rather than local-martingale status
conclusion_family: Existence or uniqueness in law of the diffusion, equivalently existence or well-posedness of the associated martingale problem, with direction fixed by the chosen primary theorem.
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: point initial condition versus arbitrary initial distribution
excluded_substitutions: a bare definition of martingale problem
only the elementary SDE-to-martingale implication when the selected source root is an equivalence or uniqueness theorem
foundation_profile: Open: classical probability, measure completion, quotient and choice usage must be audited after imports are fixed.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus pinned mathlib; exact versions and dependency closure are open.
computation_profile: No numerical computation, oracle, or native-code result is credited at intake.
primary_source_candidates: D. W. Stroock and S. R. S. Varadhan, Multidimensional Diffusion Processes, Springer, 1979, especially the chapters developing the martingale problem and uniqueness.
D. W. Stroock and S. R. S. Varadhan, Diffusion processes with continuous coefficients. I, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 22 (1969), 345-400.
D. W. Stroock and S. R. S. Varadhan, Diffusion processes with continuous coefficients. II, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 22 (1969), 479-530.
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on changes to the manifest claim, chosen source theorem, coefficient or path-space scope, Lean target, imports/toolchain, source pins, foundation/TCB policy, or rev-5.6 standard.
status_boundary: This planned intake maps the unspecialized theorem family. It does not assert an exact Lean statement, source fidelity, machine proof, or theorem completion.
